evidence.quote: Initial examination: Best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) was 20/50 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye. Both eyes had normal intraocular pressure, clear corneas, and a lens with mild cortical opacity. Fundus examination of the right eye revealed yellowish-white, granular hard exudates on the nasal and temporal sides of the fovea. Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) demonstrated a punctate hyperfluorescent lesion corresponding to the suspected hemorrhage (Figure 1B). A cross-sectional optical coherence tomography (OCT) scan through the fovea showed serous retinal detachment with dense intraretinal hard exudates (Figure 1C). A provisional diagnosis of chronic branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) was considered, despite the patient reporting no history of abnormal vision in her right eye. However, retinal artery filling time was normal

summary.text: A 68-year-old woman with hypertension for 10 years, well controlled with oral medication, and no history of diabetes mellitus or other chronic systemic disease presented to ophthalmology on April 4, 2018 with blurred vision in her right eye for over a month. Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/50 in the right eye and 20/20 in the left eye.

Right-eye fundus examination showed yellowish-white granular hard exudates beside the fovea and a suspected hemorrhagic lesion. FFA showed a punctate hyperfluorescent lesion, and OCT showed serous retinal detachment with dense intraretinal hard exudates. Retinal artery filling time was normal, cervical Doppler ultrasonography showed no significant abnormalities, and a provisional diagnosis of chronic BRVO was considered.

Intravitreal conbercept 0.5 mg/0.05 ml was given monthly for three injections. One month after the first injection BCVA in the right eye fell to 20/100 with ring-shaped hard exudates, and one month after the third it was 20/60 with a large aneurysm with white rim. The patient then declined further injections and laser treatment and did not keep the prescribed follow-up schedule.

On April 23, 2019 BCVA was 20/50 with resolved subretinal fluid and a sausage-shaped dilated flow signal on OCTA. BCVA reached 20/25 on October 22, 2019 and 20/20 in both eyes on November 27, 2020, when OCTA and OCT showed complete disappearance of the lesion. The final diagnosis was retinal capillary macroaneurysm of the right eye, which resolved spontaneously without further treatment.

oncology.note: The aneurysm is a vascular lesion; no malignancy documented.
